q: Which Act first defined 'derivatives' as 'securities' in India?
e: The 1999 amendment to the SCRA brought derivatives within the definition of 'securities', enabling derivative trading to be regulated under the existing securities framework.

q: Section 18A of SCRA states that a derivative contract is legal and valid only if:
o: It is traded on a recognised stock exchange and settled at its clearing house
Both parties have consented in writing
The underlying is a listed security
e: Section 18A: derivatives are legal only if traded on a recognised exchange AND settled through the exchange's clearing corp. Other OTC equity derivative contracts are not enforceable as securities contracts.

q: The L. C. Gupta committee report was accepted by SEBI on:
e: SEBI accepted the Gupta committee recommendations on May 11, 1998, paving the way for derivatives trading. Index futures launched June 2000.

q: Per the L. C. Gupta committee, the maximum representation of trading/clearing members on the governing council of a derivatives exchange/segment is:
e: ≤40% maximum representation of trading/clearing members on the governing council. The exchange must have a separate governing council for the derivatives segment.

q: Brokers in the derivatives segment must retain trade confirmation slips and exercise notices for at least:
e: Records must be retained for 5 years per SEBI Stock Broker Regulations. Inspections happen at least once a year.

q: A default by a derivatives broker in one segment of the exchange is treated as:
o: Default in all segments of that exchange and on all exchanges where the broker operates
e: Cross-default rule: default in one segment = default in all segments + all exchanges where the member operates. Career-ending consequence for the broker.
